text:
Every scope item is closed, and the acceptance criterion holds: one definition per
contract, with the canonical-bytes consolidation covered by laws that fail if a
second rendering diverges.

Three items were worse than recorded and one was already partly fixed; details are
in the preceding progress note.

The ScriptSource item is now resolved as far as it can be without a wire decision.
Per the chosen approach, the size question is answered once at construction:
ScriptSource.Inline has a private constructor and ByteLimit.maximumInlineScript is
the single bound, so the three prior answers (script-program decoder at 4 MiB, submit
decoder unbounded, worker's configurable limit) collapse into one that every path
inherits. There is no fixture for the submit decoder's bound because the private
constructor makes it a compile-time guarantee rather than something to sample.
Covered by core's InlineScriptBoundSuite exhaustively, plus a boundary test in
CodecBoundsLawSuite for the decoder wiring. ScriptSource became a sealed hierarchy
because an enum case cannot take a private constructor; case names and match syntax
are unchanged.

STILL DEFERRED to P6f.12, deliberately: the representation split. The submit path
carries inline bytes as a JSON array of numbers, the script-program path as base64.
Unifying them changes canonical bytes, so request digests, so attempt identities,
which invalidates existing journals. It needs a version story, not a cleanup pass.
This change was kept provably byte-neutral by leaving the encoder derived and
hand-writing only the decoder to the same shape, verified by the pinned submit
fixture and the LaunchSpec round-trip law.

512 tests pass, up from 499 when this work started.
